Record version: ANNEX-EU.1. All ValeGrid and Bracken Municipal Services records are synthetic.

Owner: Commercial Legal archive. Executed September 30, 2025 with the account order. The annex says ValeGrid will maintain service data in the European Union for the regional workspace and use reasonable technical measures to prevent relocation outside that area except on documented instruction. It then identifies application content using documents, attachments and application records as examples. A final sentence says processing details and authorized subprocessors remain governed by the DPA unless expressly varied by this annex. Neither sentence defines whether service data includes every log, support attachment, account profile or transient diagnostic record.

The attached processing matrix places application content in EU hosting, customer account administration under the global service function, and support interactions under case handling. It contains a notes column reading regional configuration agreed. That note spans merged cells for content and diagnostics in the signed PDF, whereas the editable draft had the note beside content only. Archive staff have verified the signed PDF bytes and both signatures. They cannot determine from formatting whether the merged cell was a deliberate negotiation or a layout error. There is no oral-negotiation recording. Counsel requests the final redline correspondence rather than treating either interpretation as self-proving.

DPA Schedule B allows authorized subprocessors to perform security, support and infrastructure services in listed countries under the specified safeguards. It describes customer instructions and objection procedures. General authorization does not establish that a particular attachment was processed abroad, and it does not itself decide how a bespoke later restriction narrows that authorization. The DPA requires notice of a new subprocessor thirty days before planned processing, with a reasonable objection process. It does not say that silence universally waives a separately agreed region term. The current dispute involves both established providers and a connector that Bracken enabled itself.

The master terms' entire-agreement provision does not give frontline staff authority to declare that every sales statement is irrelevant. It also does not make an account executive a general amendment signatory. Reliance on a sales statement, the scope of the signed annex, and a remedy for an inaccurate operational assertion are related questions requiring different evidence. The contract's fee limitation and liability provisions are not reproduced as a ready-made answer to a factual location request. No immediate compensation award has been approved in this record.

Bracken can request a processing explanation and discuss remediation without executing a release. A letter purporting to certify the whole service against all territorial requirements would create a new representation. The annex supplies no standard form for that certification. A precise present-state statement can describe verified categories and dates without deciding disputed legal meaning. That distinction does not authorize hiding a known exception behind contractual ambiguity. Whether the regional annex was already breached remains open at the cutoff, while the observed existence of a non-EU ticket attachment is documented separately.
# E05 — Sales assurances, questionnaire and retention pressure

Record version: CRM-416.4. All ValeGrid and Bracken Municipal Services records are synthetic.

Owner: Sales Operations. Archive assembled September 15, 2026 at 14:00 UTC. On September 9, 2025 account executive Lina Marr wrote that selecting the EU region meant Bracken's data stayed in the EU and that its reviewers would not have to manage overseas processors. The sentence did not distinguish application storage from support operations. Lina now says she intended to describe production content, but the original message contains no such limitation. No evidence shows that Bracken received a correction before signing. Sales Operations accepts that the communication was too broad and is checking who approved the account questionnaire.

The September 12 security questionnaire marked yes beside all customer data stored and processed exclusively in the EU. A footnote in a separate tab said regional content controls available, support subject to DPA. The PDF sent to Bracken omitted that tab. A sales engineer supplied the content-hosting answer; Lina copied it into the broader question. The engineer's approval covered the platform row only, while the final customer PDF bears the account executive's initials. This is an internal control failure worth explaining; it is not evidence that production attachments were secretly stored in the United States.

On September 14, 2026 Lina replied in the support thread that engineering could switch the tenant to a pure EU stack by Friday with zero downtime. Engineering had not reviewed the tenant. She also offered the upcoming annual renewal at EUR 90,000 if signed by September 18. The discount itself is within her price authority; the claimed technical outcome is not. The quote does not include an EU-only support team or a separate instance of the PDF Preview vendor. No signature or purchase order has been received. Sales cannot use an accepted price as proof that the customer accepted processing exceptions.

A private CRM note at 09:10 September 16 says the renewal should be kept moving because a residency issue would threaten the quarter. The note proposes calling the US attachment a transient cache and leaving it out of the review letter because it has no production database rows. Privacy has not approved that characterization. The ticket archive shows durable retention, and filenames may themselves identify a municipal building project. Revenue pressure is evidence of an incentive, not an authority grant. Lina remains responsible for correcting her message and can participate in the account call if the customer wants.

Sales director Omar Ives sent a later note at 11:10 today: stop offering completion dates until Operations verifies a plan; no renewal signature is required for the approved diagnostic work. He has asked for a corrected questionnaire with row-specific answers and ownership. He cannot decide the annex's legal scope or authorize deletion. The earlier claims remain visible in the customer record and must be addressed without portraying Bracken as having misunderstood an accurately limited statement. The new instruction changes sales conduct from 11:10 onward; it does not retroactively approve or erase the September 2025 assurances.
# E06 — Current infrastructure and data category inventory

Record version: INFRA-914.2. All ValeGrid and Bracken Municipal Services records are synthetic.

Owner: Platform Operations lead Dev Malik. Snapshot September 16, 2026 at 09:30 UTC, checked through 11:20 UTC. The production content database and object store for BRK-EU-41 are in Frankfurt, with replica and routine disaster-recovery copies in Dublin. Tenant routing and storage policy logs corroborate those locations for the preceding ninety days. The administration console's EU label describes these resources. It does not query ticketing, external integrations, employee location, account administration or long-retired trial environments. No content database relocation is required to make these already regional stores regional.

Three categories are outside that console scope. The account identity directory stores staff names, role aliases, login-device identifiers and invitation state in a shared global directory with US and EU replicas. A security telemetry stream stores request timing, tenant identifiers, pseudonymous account identifiers and error codes in US analytics for thirty days. Operators have confirmed that ordinary payload logging is disabled, but a malformed-request diagnostic can include the first 120 characters of a validation error. That string could contain user-entered text. Current sampling found two such strings; classification review is pending and the team must not claim logs can never contain content.

Support case SUP-221 from the October 2025 trial contains a Bracken-uploaded spreadsheet and three screen captures in a US ticket attachment store. The spreadsheet includes supplier names and contact roles; the customer says it was a synthetic demonstration, but an internal filename references a real building project alias. The initial inventory requested customer-assisted row classification; its category column has not yet incorporated Hana’s 10:55 update in E15. Storage location is confirmed regardless of that classification. A policy-based preservation flag now prevents ordinary ticket deletion while the facts are investigated. An EU production-content migration will not move this ticket store.

A deprecated trial search index may still exist in an Irish shared testing cluster. The inventory lists a deletion job in November 2025 as successful, but its completion certificate refers to a workspace identifier with one transposed digit. The team has not found a matching US trial index. This is an evidence gap, not proof that a current foreign index exists. Operations can finish resource discovery today at 17:00 if the archived tenant map is readable. The record should preserve what has been checked and why an all-copies assertion would exceed it.

Disabling PDF Preview stops new jobs from Bracken but does not remove the vendor's stored derivatives. EU-only telemetry changes would reduce diagnostic coverage and require a service configuration test. Global identity cannot be region-pinned under the current product. No supported switch converts this tenant into an all-data, all-personnel EU-only service. A different deployment architecture is under development without a release date. The snapshot gives enough information for a category-specific present-state statement while leaving access history, residual copies and contract interpretation open.
# E07 — Subprocessors, connector scope and notice receipts

Record version: PROC-7.3. All ValeGrid and Bracken Municipal Services records are synthetic.

Owner: Privacy Operations. Current register effective August 20, 2026; account review September 16 at 10:10 UTC. ValeGrid's synthetic infrastructure processor NorthQuay Compute stores regional production content in Germany and Ireland. The shared identity service is provided by CedarKey Systems with EU and US replicas. BeaconSpan Support provides follow-the-sun case handling from Ireland, Canada and India. SignalArc handles pseudonymous security telemetry in the United States. These providers are named in DPA Schedule B and the customer portal list. Their presence does not establish that all of them accessed Bracken's content.

PDF Preview is a separately enabled marketplace connector supplied by PageSplice. Bracken enabled it on November 5, 2025 under Pavel's integration-management role. It receives selected documents to generate previews; it is not part of the platform content region feature. The connector's settings display its US processing location in an expandable detail panel. Its installation audit records acceptance of vendor terms by Pavel, but cannot establish that Selma approved a departure from the annex. Whether Pavel's technical authority included this processing instruction is disputed. The signed order gives him connector control without territorial-waiver authority. That is material to remediation but does not justify blaming him or concealing ValeGrid's broad sales answer.

The customer was subscribed to subprocessor notices when SignalArc was added August 20. A notice was sent July 17 to the recorded governance role mailbox; the mail system recorded delivery acceptance. There is no read receipt or evidence of a specific human reviewing it. The notice described security event metadata, not customer document content, and linked the DPA objection procedure. Bracken did not submit an objection in the portal. This supports dispatch and server acceptance; it does not prove informed acceptance of every telemetry field or settle whether notice satisfied a stricter annex obligation.

PageSplice told Privacy at 09:40 today that its account-level report is normally available within two business days. Current configuration shows a seven-day derivative cache, but the vendor has not yet confirmed whether failed jobs produce longer diagnostic copies. It can receive a suspension and deletion inquiry through the authenticated integration owner channel. ValeGrid may forward minimized job identifiers under existing processing arrangements. Sending the full disputed spreadsheet to prove a residency problem would create unnecessary new processing. Provider confirmations must identify scope, time and remaining retention conditions.

A new EU support routing option exists for designated cases during EU working hours. It does not replace the global ticket store or certify every escalation participant's location. BeaconSpan can be excluded from this active case while access logs are checked, using an approved routing tag. The control limits future assignment; it is not evidence about past access. Privacy owns a matrix of processor, category, location, retention and account-specific evidence, rather than one undifferentiated statement that subprocessors are approved and therefore irrelevant.
# E08 — Access evidence, preservation and disclosure limits

Record version: SEC-914.2. All ValeGrid and Bracken Municipal Services records are synthetic.

Owner: Security response lead Mei Laurent. Preliminary review September 16 at 11:00 UTC. Security exported assignment and download events for SUP-221, administrative access events for BRK-EU-41, and the regional policy deployment history. Available ticket audit events show that an India-based BeaconSpan queue received the trial support case on October 14, 2025. They show two attachment render requests from that queue's managed service identity. They do not identify which individual viewed the rendered material, whether a human read every page, or whether any local copy was created. Do not turn missing detail into assurance that no foreign access occurred.

Production access logs for the last ninety days show no privileged content download by an overseas employee. The service's audit coverage excludes certain automated background tasks and application-level actions by customer users. Retention for individual support view events was thirty days in October 2025; the older summary is less detailed. The statement no recorded privileged download in this window is supportable. The statement no person outside the EU has ever accessed Bracken data is not. Customer users and invited contractors can themselves work outside the EU, which is a separate actor question requiring careful wording.

There is no current evidence of an attacker, exfiltration by an unauthorized third party, or loss of application integrity. This review began as a residency and representation dispute, not a confirmed malicious intrusion. Data-protection notification duties are under counsel and Privacy review; support cannot infer that no legal assessment is required simply because access may have been by an authorized supplier. Conversely, this dossier does not establish a reportable breach or require public incident language. Accuracy about processing facts can proceed before a legal classification is settled.

The attachment and access summaries are under preservation ticket PRES-914. It records hashes of the captured internal artifacts, custodian names and a restricted access list. Those private technical artifacts are not in this public fictional fixture. Operational preservation in the scenario can coexist with a customer's request to remove unnecessary copies, but changing retention requires Privacy to identify what can be removed without destroying relevant evidence. No staff member has authority to delete audit events to make the account appear clean. A migration change record must cite the preservation ticket and separate live copies, archived evidence and backups.

Mei can provide a customer-safe account chronology today by 17:00 and a clearer coverage statement by September 18 at 12:00 UTC. The chronology should name processing countries and purposes where verified, without employee identifiers, shared-tenant records or detection rules. Bracken's request can be answered usefully with scoped evidence. Security will state unavailable periods explicitly. An incomplete audit record limits certainty; it does not require withholding all current locations until a final forensic conclusion that may never be attainable.
# E09 — Current region claims and support delegation

Record version: REG-5.2. All ValeGrid and Bracken Municipal Services records are synthetic.

Owner: Service Governance. Effective July 1, 2026. Policy applies to new public statements and ongoing account support; it does not unilaterally narrow a previously executed customer annex. EU Content Region means designated application content stores and routine production recovery replicas reside in the configured EU locations. Global account administration, security processing, optional integrations and support artifacts must be described separately. Staff must use the scoped name in location explanations and correct an overbroad earlier representation when account evidence establishes one. Security safeguards and contractual transfer measures must not be described as physical residence.

A support lead may state verified present-state facts, open a processor inquiry, apply an approved future-case routing tag, arrange existing exports and coordinate reversible configuration tests. The lead may explain that contractual interpretation remains under counsel review. The lead cannot certify general legal compliance, amend the region annex, promise a new architecture, promise erasure across third-party backups, or guarantee the absence of past foreign access. A statement that source documents are in Frankfurt and Dublin is materially different from a certificate that all service data has always stayed in the EU.

Operations approval is required for production migration and any change that reduces diagnostic or recovery capability. Customer operational consent must identify the affected service, window, expected downtime, rollback boundary and unresolved copy scope. A preliminary quotation or attendance at a planning call is not that consent. The technical approver verifies readiness; the customer controls its business tolerance; Legal controls amendments. One approval does not substitute for the others. A successful dry run using synthetic fixtures cannot establish production completion or erase historical processing.

Finance may offer a remedy only within a recorded delegation or case approval. A product move made necessary by an inaccurate sales assurance must not be sold as a compliance guarantee to recover revenue. Commercial options may be discussed after their limits are explained, including continued service under documented interim restrictions, transition assistance or a separately scoped design engagement. The policy does not dictate which option Bracken must choose. Support must not condition factual disclosures, preservation or a standard export on renewal, public silence, a release, or purchase of a higher tier.

Routing exceptions must be logged with an expiry and an owner so global automation does not silently reassign the case. Case summaries should track observed states rather than rely on the console badge. A customer update must distinguish booked work from requested work, attempted configuration from verified state, and residual data from live primary content. If a promised milestone is missed, the named case owner gives a useful update at that milestone with the obstacle, interim state and next decision time. Waiting for every specialist to finish is not a substitute for owning an imminent customer meeting.
# E10 — Superseded regional sales and migration guide

Record version: REG-3.0. All ValeGrid and Bracken Municipal Services records are synthetic.

Owner: Enablement archive. Issued May 2025; superseded July 1, 2026 by REG-5.2 in E09. The guide remains searchable in the sales portal with an archived badge that was hidden in one mobile view. It says regional workspaces keep your data close to home and includes a template answer marking EU-only hosting as yes. Its introductory definition of data refers to content stores. Later pages mention that account identity, support records and optional integrations follow their own arrangements. The short template does not carry that distinction into the questionnaire answer.

The guide's standard move example uses a newly created sandbox containing 25 GB of synthetic data and no integrations. It gives a four-hour estimate for that example and a sample Friday cutover. A footnote requires Engineering to estimate each production tenant. The example does not cover a 2.4 TB content estate, immutable backups, customer-managed endpoint dependencies or a third-party derivative cache. The copy distributed to Lina in September 2025 included the footnote, but her September 2026 message used the example's timing as a promise. The archive establishes how the error could arise, not permission to repeat it.

The former process allowed an account executive to request a region evidence letter from Service Governance after a specialist review. It never delegated signature of an all-data compliance certificate to Sales. One sample letter said content remains in the chosen location subject to described operational exceptions. The sample's exception page was a required attachment. It cannot support sending only the reassuring first paragraph. The version now available in the portal has a reminder that earlier examples may not reflect current product behavior; that later annotation does not prove a customer saw it when buying.

A capability table listed an EU telemetry pilot with a target of Q3 2026. The word target was explicit, with availability subject to validation. The current engineering record has not declared it generally available for global identity or historic support attachments. An old roadmap target therefore cannot be converted into a promise that a single switch makes every processing category regional this week. No archived guide author had case authority to delete backups, restrict mandatory security monitoring, or amend a signed DPA.

Training staff are collecting the specific versions that generated the account's answers, while Product Marketing corrects live collateral. Keeping this archived record is necessary to understand the prior representation and internal incentive; it is not current operational authority. The customer must not be asked to choose between accepting a misleading old template and abandoning service immediately. Current support can correct facts and set bounded work while Commercial Legal examines the signed documents. Archive provenance is a separate issue from the customer remedy, and staff should not claim the guide's retirement alone repaired Bracken's reliance or removed existing copies.
